rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form faʿlā from ḥusn, used for a single blessing or act of kindness.
rows.anchor: الحسنى : فعلى من الحسن ، يقال : في النعمة الواحدة ، أو الفعلة الواحدة من الإحسان .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes give al-ḥusnā the sense of Paradise in these three passages.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الجنة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes also use al-ḥusnā for sons in the statement that the speakers claim to have sons.
rows.anchor: والثاني : البنون ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Here al-ḥusnā means good: the claimants say they intended nothing but good.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الخير ، ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: أحمد ابن حنبل
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā means compensation or return; Ibn Hanbal is cited, while some attach this sense to Paradise.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الخلف ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الليل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the verse about God’s names, al-ḥusnā means the highest or most exalted.
rows.anchor: والخامس : العليا ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In the command concerning parents, ḥusnan means kindness or dutiful goodness.
rows.anchor: والسادس : البر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في العنكبوت والأحقاف

rows.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: Ali b. ʿUbayd Allah defines shifāʾ as what suits the soul by removing harm; here it means joy in believers’ hearts.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الشفاء ، ملائم النفس بما يزيل عنها الأذى .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second Qurʾanic sense of shifāʾ is recovery or sound health.
rows.anchor: والثاني : العافية . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is clarification, illustrated by healing for what is in people’s breasts and for believers.
rows.anchor: والثالث : البيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The source’s teacher defines shaqāʾ as the strength of causes of affliction and al-shaqī as the most afflicted person.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا : الشقاء : قوة أسباب البلاء . والشقي : أعظم أهل البلاء .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of shaqāʾ is toil, including the statements that the Prophet was not burdened with the Qurʾan and the follower will not suffer.
rows.anchor: أحدها : التعب . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في سورة طه )

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense of shaqāʾ is disobedience, as in Jesus’ statement that he was not made a tyrant or disobedient.
rows.anchor: والثاني : العصيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is unbelief: the wretched person is an unbeliever, contrasted with the believer.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الكفر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah derives from baqāʾ; al-bāqī persists through successive times, while baqiyyah is what remains when its company disappears at once.
rows.anchor: البقية مشتقة من البقاء . والباقي : ما تكررت عليه الأزمان وهو باق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs use baqā in place of baqiya; yubqī can mean to watch or keep something under observation.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول : بقى مكان بقي . يقال : فلان يبقي الشيء إذا رقبه ورصده .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith uses abqaynā rasūl Allāh to mean that the Companions waited for the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( وأبقينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ) . يعني انتظرناه .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Baqiyyah here means a small number of people who would forbid corruption.
rows.anchor: أحدها : القليل ، ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Baqiyyah can mean permanence: what is with God endures, and what is with people passes away.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الدوام ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: It can mean a remnant of something that has gone, as with what remained from the household of Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: والثالث : ما بقي من الذاهب ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Baqiyyat Allāh means God’s reward; al-Yazidi instead glosses it as His obedience.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الثواب ، ومنه قوله تعالى ( 33 / أ ) في هود

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetes take al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt to mean the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الصلوات الخمس ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies the enduring righteous deeds as formulae praising and declaring God’s oneness and greatness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد بها سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lولا originally prevents one thing because another exists: were it not for disobedience, one would have been treated well.
rows.anchor: ' لولا ' ( في الأصل ) : حرف وضع لامتناع الشيء لوجود غيره

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic use means halā, an urging or rebuke such as ‘why did they not humble themselves?’
rows.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى ' هلا ' ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second use means ‘there was not’; some scholars treat it as a form of the preceding halā sense.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى لم يكن . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In its original conditional use, the clause says that without God’s grace and mercy the hearers would have been losers.
rows.anchor: والثالث : وقوعها على أصلها وهو وضعها لامتناع الشيء لوجود غيره

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Jonah’s being among those who glorified God prevented his remaining in the fish until resurrection; this is another original conditional use of lولا.
rows.anchor: وفي الصافات : ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين للبث

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says lولا without a response means halā, but when it has a response it does not carry that meaning.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة إذا رأيت ' لولا ' بلا جواب فهي بمعنى : هلا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines rawḥ as comfort and a pleasant breeze; it can mean mercy because the soul’s relief comes through mercy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الروح : الراحة وطيب النسيم . وقد تكون الروح في القرآن : الرحمة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris glosses rawḥ as a breeze, rawāḥ as the period from the sun’s decline until night, and marāḥ as livestock’s nighttime shelter; he also explains related uses for a shallow bowl, comfort, and a wind passage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس : الروح : نسيم الريح . والرواح : من زوال الشمس إلى الليل

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A line attributed to ʿUmar compares a camel’s rider to a branch in an airy place, illustrating mirwaḥah and breeze imagery.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه ركب ناقة فمشت به مشيا جيدا فقال

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Qurʾanic sense of rawḥ is mercy, as in the prohibition on despairing of God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الرحمة . ( 59 / ب ) ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Rawḥ means rest or comfort in the reading that opens the rāʾ in the promise of repose and provision.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الراحة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الواقعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses khizy as humiliation.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : الخزي : الإهانة .

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says khaziya means to fall into a calamity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت : خزي يخزى خزيا : إذا وقع في بلية .

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines the disgraced person as humbled and despised by a binding proof; to disgrace someone is to bind him with proof and humble him.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : المخزى في اللغة : المذل المحقور بأمر قد لزمه بحجة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris gives khizy the senses of banishment and hatred; khaziya can also mean that a man felt ashamed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : معنى الخزي : الإبعاد والمقت . وخزي الرجل : استحيى خزاية

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is disgrace and humiliation, illustrated by passages about punishment, worldly torment, and the wicked.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الذل والهوان . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is public shame or scandal, as Lot asks not to be shamed concerning his guests.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الفضيحة . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is punishment, including that of the Day and God’s punishment in worldly life.
rows.anchor: والثالث : العذاب . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fourth sense is killing and exile: the worldly disgrace of Banū Qurayẓah and al-Naḍīr, and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith’s death at Badr.
rows.anchor: والرابع : القتل والجلاء . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾ is whatever causes distress; the pudendum is called sawʾah because exposing it causes distress.
rows.anchor: السوء : ما يسوء . وسميت العورة سوأة : لأن كشفها يسوء .

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes state that al-sūʾ has eleven Qurʾanic senses; this excerpt gives the first nine.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السوء في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first sense is severity or hardship, including severe punishment and an evil reckoning.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الشدة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is illicit sex or sexual misconduct in the cited story and description.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الزنى . ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is harming or crippling the she-camel sent as a sign.
rows.anchor: والثالث : العقر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف وهود والشعراء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth sense is leprosy, excluded in descriptions of the hand coming out white.
rows.anchor: والرابع : البرص . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه والنمل والقصص

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fifth sense is punishment, which God may intend for a people and from which the God-fearing are saved.
rows.anchor: والخامس : العذاب ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The sixth sense is idolatry or unbelief, illustrated by denials of wrongdoing, acting in ignorance, and those who did evil.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الشرك . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

words: مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ إِيمَٰنِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the passage concerns Jabr, a slave of ʿĀmir al-Ḥaḍramī, whom his master forced to disbelieve while his heart remained faithful.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت في جبر غلام عامر بن الحضرمي . أكرهه على الكفر وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The seventh sense is insult or abusive speech, whether spoken openly or directed against believers.
rows.anchor: والسابع : الشتم . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The eighth sense is harm or adversity that may touch a person or be removed by God.
rows.anchor: الثامن : الضر . ( 77 / أ ) ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The ninth sense is sin, especially sin committed in ignorance for which repentance is accepted.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : الذنب . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadl means fairness and right, opposite of injustice; an approved just person is called ʿadl, an invariant verbal noun in gender and number.
rows.anchor: العدل : الإنصاف والحق . وضده : الجور . ويقال للمرضي من الناس : عدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿadl can mean an equivalent or ransom; ʿadaltu something also means that I straightened it until it stood upright.
rows.anchor: والعدل : المثل . وبسط الوالي عدله ومعدلته وعدلت الشيء فاعتدل

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is ransom or compensation, which cannot be accepted on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الفداء . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is equitable treatment, especially fairness between wives.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الإنصاف . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third sense is the value or equivalent of the penalty, paid through fasting.
rows.anchor: والثالث : القيمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fourth sense is associating partners with God, as unbelievers make equals with their Lord.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الشرك . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some interpret the command to justice as tawḥīd, the confession that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: والخامس : التوحيد . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: Abu Zakariya classifies mā as either a noun or particle; as a noun, it can be the nonrelative predicate in an exclamation.
rows.anchor: في الكلام على ضربين : اسم وحرف ، فإذا كانت اسما فهي على خمسة أقسام

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: Mā may be a relative noun meaning ‘that which,’ as in what people possess passing away and what God possesses enduring.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن تكون خبرا بمعنى الذي موصولة

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: As a noun, mā can also be interrogative, conditional, or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن تكون استفهاما . نحو : ما عندك ؟

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: In ‘a parable, mā a mosquito,’ mā may be indefinite or extra; with baʿūḍah nominative it can be relative, as in ‘this is a thing ready with me.’
rows.anchor: والخامس : أن تكون نكرة موصوفة . نحو قوله

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: As a particle, mā may be extra, negative, a verbal noun, or a particle that prevents its preceding word from governing.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت حرفا فهي على أربعة أقسام

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: In inna-mā and rubba-mā, mā is kāffah: it prevents inna and rubba from operating on what follows.
rows.anchor: والرابع : أن تكون كافة عن العمل . نحو

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says mā and man share an origin: man is used for people, while mā is used for other things.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : ' ما ' و ' من ' أصلها واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr is compensation received under a contract for the use of benefits; to hire someone is to assign a wage for an act.
rows.anchor: الأجر : العوض المأخوذ في العقد على المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr also means setting a bone; ijār is a roof without a surrounding barrier, with plural forms ajājīr and ajājirah, and injār is a variant.
rows.anchor: والأجر أيضا : جبر العظم . تقول

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of ajr is payment for nursing a child.
rows.anchor: أحدها : نفقة الرضاع . ومنه قوله تعالى ' في الطلاق '

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is a bride’s marriage payment or dowry.
rows.anchor: والثاني : المهر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense is payment or a fee, including compensation the Prophet says he did not ask from people.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الجعل . ومنه قوله تعالى في سبأ

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth sense is reward for obedience, promised to those who are patient according to their best deeds.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الثواب على الطاعة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exegetes add favorable praise bestowed in this world as a fifth sense.
rows.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجهين آخرين : أحدهما : الثناء الحسن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exegetes add Paradise as another sense of ajr, citing the promise of a great reward.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الجنة . ومنه قوله في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first sense of ḥattā is ‘until,’ marking an endpoint in these passages.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى ' إلى ' ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is ‘when’ or ‘then, when,’ introducing the next event in a sequence.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى ' فلما ' ، ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third sense is ‘so that’ or ‘in order that,’ as in waiting until the prescribed term is completed.
rows.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى ' كي ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fourth sense is the conjunction ‘and,’ linking God’s testing with making known the patient and those who strive.
rows.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى ' الواو ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijāb is a barrier that prevents perception; a blind person is called screened because something blocks sight.
rows.anchor: الحجاب : الحاجز المانع من الإدراك . ويقال للأعمى : محجوب

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of ḥijāb is a partition between two groups.
rows.anchor: أحدها : السور ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is a curtain or screen, as in Mary’s screen from her people and the screen behind which wives are addressed.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الستر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The third sense of ḥijāb is a mountain that hides something from view.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الجبل ، ومنه قوله تعالى [ في ص ]

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth sense is being barred or prevented, as unbelievers are barred from their Lord.
rows.anchor: والرابع : المنع ، ومنه قوله تعالى في المطففين

none: Colophon and completion verses only; no explanation of the scoped verse.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj lists four language senses of salām: the verbal noun of salima, a plural of salāmah, one of God’s names, and a tree.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : سمعت محمد بن يزيد يذكر أن السلام في اللغة أربعة أشياء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: As a verbal noun, salām is a prayer that a person be safe in religion, self, and property: release from harm.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : ومعنى السلام الذي هو مصدر سلمت أنه : دعاء للإنسان أن يسلم من الآفات

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: As a divine name, al-Salām means the possessor of peace, who owns safety as release from harm.
rows.anchor: والسلام الذي هو اسم الله [ تعالى ] تأويله ذو السلام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The tree called salām is large and strong; the author thinks its name may reflect freedom from afflictions.
rows.anchor: فأما السلام الشجر فهو شجر عظام قوي أحسبه سمي بذلك لسلامته من الآفات

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Stones are called salām for their hardness; peace names reconciliation because it means safety from evil, while a ladder carries one where desired.
rows.anchor: وأما السلام : الحجارة فسميت بذلك : لسلامتها من الرخاوة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is a name of God, illustrated by paths or the abode of al-Salām and the divine name.
rows.anchor: أحدها : اسم من أسماء الله عز وجل . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second Qurʾanic sense is the familiar greeting of peace.
rows.anchor: والثاني : التحية المعروفة . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الأنعام ]

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third Qurʾanic sense is safety from every evil, as in promises of peace and protection.
rows.anchor: والثالث : السلامة من كل شر . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fourth sense is goodness; Ibn Qutayba glosses the salām of the Night of Decree as ‘good.’
rows.anchor: والرابع : الخير . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في هود ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwāh is the plural of fam, whose underlying form is fawh; fawh means breadth of mouth, and fāha means to utter words.
rows.anchor: الأفواه : واحدها فم . وأصل الفم فوه على وزن فوز . والفوه : سعة الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mufawwah is someone capable of speaking; an anonymous poem says the devout may restrain a tongue of foolish speech despite being eloquent.
rows.anchor: قد يخزن الورع التقي لسانه … هذر الكلام وإنه لمفوه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is literal mouths; the messengers’ opponents put their hands to their mouths to silence them with abuse.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الأفواه المعروفة التي واحدها فم ، ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Afwāh can mean tongues; this is metonymy by adjacency or cause, like calling the intellect a heart because the heart contains it.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الألسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some add speech as a third sense: opponents try to extinguish God’s light with their words.
rows.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم ' وجها ' ثالثا فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaff ordinarily means one person standing beside another; maṣaff is a battle position and maṣāff its plural. Ṣafṣaf is flat ground.
rows.anchor: الصف في التعارف : وقوف الشخص إلى جنب الشخص . والمصف : الموقف في الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣafīf is meat prepared for travel, either boiled or roasted, and the anonymous poem uses it for such meat.
rows.anchor: فظل طهاة اللحم من بين منضج … صفيف شواء أو قدير معجل

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense is a row or rank, as in God’s love for fighters aligned in a row and ranks of those who line up.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الصف المعروف . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الصف

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is a gathered assembly or crowd, including those presented before their Lord and the magicians arriving together.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الجمع . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth listed use of hal is ‘is it not?’ or an affirmative question.
rows.anchor: والخامس : بمعنى ' أليس ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth use is a command: ‘look down’ or ‘go and see.’
rows.anchor: والسادس : بمعنى الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventh use is a request or question; ‘Is there any more?’ means ‘Give me more.’
rows.anchor: والسابع : بمعنى السؤال . ومنه قوله تعالى في ق

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The sixteenth listed sense of dhikr is the ʿAṣr prayer, in Solomon’s statement about loving horses over remembrance of his Lord.
rows.anchor: والسادس عشر : صلاة العصر . ومنه قوله تعالى في ص

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The seventeenth sense of dhikr is the unseen; the unbelievers ask whether this is the one who mentions their gods.
rows.anchor: والسابع عشر : الغيب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنبياء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The eighteenth sense is the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: والثامن عشر : اللوح المحفوظ . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنبياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say al-zabūr in this verse means all the earlier books.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد بالزبور ها هنا سائر الكتب

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The nineteenth sense is praise of God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: والتاسع عشر : الثناء على الله ( سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The twentieth sense of dhikr is the Messenger, in the statement that God sent down a reminder, namely a messenger.
rows.anchor: والعشرون : الرسول . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الطلاق ]

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: In the cited phrase about sending down a reminder, anzala is understood to mean arsala, ‘sent.’
rows.anchor: قيل : إن أنزل ها هنا بمعنى أرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubūr is the plural of zabūr, a book; al-Zajjaj says a zabūr is any book containing wisdom. Zabartu al-kitāb means ‘I wrote the book.’
rows.anchor: الزبر : جمع زبور . والزبور : الكتاب . وقال الزجاج : الزبور كل كتاب ذو حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related forms also mean chest, a piece of iron, a calamity, rebuking someone, and one’s writing.
rows.anchor: والزبرة : الصدرة - وزبرة الحديد : قطعة منه . والزبير : الداهية . وزبرت الرجل : انتهرته

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of zubur is pieces: the people split their affair into separate divisions.
rows.anchor: أحدها : القطع . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The second sense is books or scriptures, including the statement that the Qurʾan is found in the books of the ancients.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإنه لفي زبر الأولين ﴾

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The third sense is David’s Psalter, named alongside God’s writing about the righteous inheriting the earth.
rows.anchor: والثالث : كتاب داود . ومنه قوله تعالى ( 66 / ب ) في الأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fourth sense is the Preserved Tablet, where everything they did is recorded.
rows.anchor: والرابع : اللوح المحفوظ . ومنه قوله تعالى في القمر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The fifth sense is reports or histories of earlier peoples, cited with the clear proofs sent to messengers.
rows.anchor: والخامس : ^ ( أخبار الأمم
